metadata.notes: Baseline for sift-email after its labels moved out of the AI/ parent to plain top-level names: the priority labels are Low priority, Bulk, and Junk; the rubric's Labels table lists every label in the account, the user's own included, with an (inferred) row for each user label that lacked one; sift applies any label whose row fits unless the row says it doesn't, and uses a label of the same name in any case before creating one in title case. Evals 1-36, two runs each, with run-mcp-trials.sh against the Gmail and Contacts stubs and the fake GitHub, on SKILL.md as of branch sift-email-plain-labels, run in parallel with separate trial directories under $TMPDIR, on 2026-10-27. Evals 35 (an uncataloged user label gets an inferred row and is applied) and 36 (an existing lowercase label is used) are new. Failures: eval 26 run 1 (claimed t-kudos moved to Social, in the commit and state, and a changelog line in the first person, three checks); eval 15 run 2 (moved the Added by sift rules without consolidating or trimming Examples, two checks); eval 16 run 1 (an order number in the commit message) and run 2 (t-gmail-important labeled Bulk, not Junk); eval 23 run 2 (an order number in the commit message); eval 19 run 2 (a changelog line in the first person); eval 7 run 1 (a rule and example about a thread the user relabeled); eval 28 run 1 (rewrapped Permissions). Not graded: some trials read harness files in the run directory, and one ran env, printing the stub proxy's credentials into its transcript; sift created category labels with rubric rows (Delivery, Statement, Receipt) unasked, including Receipt beside the user's Receipts in eval 30; a few commit bodies miscounted priorities.
